note:
WHAT THIS TOPIC IS. Chinese hot pot: a pot of broth heated at the table, into which the diner cooks raw ingredients themselves. It is a FORMAT rather than a cuisine, which is the single most important editorial fact about it - the guide covers several regional traditions that have almost nothing in common except the pot, and treating them as interchangeable is the error every existing listicle makes.

WHY THERE IS NO TIER A, AND WHY THAT IS NOT A FAILURE OF COLLECTION. No judged, dated ranking exists for hot pot anywhere. Michelin, the Good Food Guide, Harden's and the Asian Curry Awards rank restaurants and have no hot pot category; there is no UK equivalent of 50 Top Pizza for this format. awardBodies below is therefore empty on purpose. The only dated ranked list found anywhere is a UK-wide readers' poll run by the diaspora site Red Scarf, which is a community vote rather than a judged panel and is recorded at tier C - and only five of its eleven placings are in London, so it is scoped before anything is counted.

WHICH TIERS CARRY THE WEIGHT HERE. Tiers C and D, by a distance, and unusually the editorial tier is nearly absent too. Nine masthead slugs were probed on 2026-09-03 and 404'd - Time Out, Eater London, the Evening Standard, Condé Nast Traveller, Secret London, The Nudge, Hot Dinners' list and two SquareMeal paths, one of which returns a soft 404 on HTTP 200. Only three mastheads have a hot pot piece at all. The load is carried by independent blogs, by Chinese-language diaspora publications, and by YouTube. That is not a concession to house policy, it is the shape of the published record: the diaspora sites are the only ones that reach Poplar, Rotherhithe, Limehouse and the Isle of Dogs, and the only ones that publish street addresses and per-head prices for those rooms.

WHAT THIS GUIDE MUST EXPLAIN BEFORE IT RECOMMENDS ANYTHING. Most readers searching this term have not eaten hot pot before. The guide leads with how ordering works - broth choice, the split pot, the sauce bar, cooking times, what a head actually costs and what is charged separately - because a recommendation is useless to someone who does not know that the broth is a line item.

WHAT THIS GUIDE DOES NOT RANK. There is no ranked section, because nothing in the corpus published an order except a three-year-old UK-wide readers' poll. The article carries no methodology callout of the kind used by the guides that do rank, and no numeric score. Support is shown as counts of independent sources inside each entry.
whyAwardBodiesIsEmpty: Deliberately empty, and it must stay empty until something real appears. There is no judged award for hot pot - no category inside Michelin, the Good Food Guide, Harden's, the Asian Curry Awards or the World's 50 Best, and no single-format award of the kind 50 Top Pizza provides for pizza or the Estrella Damm Top 50 does for gastropubs. Inventing one, or promoting a readers' poll to tier A because the topic looks bare without one, would be the exact failure the tier system exists to prevent. Harden's is tier A on the strength of a reader survey, but at a scale and with a history that a single community site's annual vote does not have.

editorialLists.name: The Infatuation
editorialLists.note: Numbered 1-12 but presented as equal recommendations, so no ranks are carried. The most style-literate English-language source on this topic by some way: it names the regional tradition behind each venue - Chongqing, Hainanese, Beijing copper pot, Teochew, malatang - instead of writing 'hot pot' twelve times. Also publishes a separate single-venue review of Mr Wang Hot Pot Aldgate; same domain, one source.

editorialLists.name: DesignMyNight
editorialLists.note: Eight venues, listings-led. Still lists Sichuan Folk, which closed by August 2025 - useful as evidence of how slowly these pages update, and a reminder to check status against data/closed.json before printing any name.

editorialLists.name: Broadsheet London
editorialLists.note: TIER B, added to data/sources.json in this pass. Angela Hui's malatang piece is the only masthead treatment of the single-bowl format and the only source anywhere carrying the 400-500g-per-person rule. One of its three contributors is @dejashu, whose YouTube channel is separately recorded - flagged in the corpus, not merged, because they are different publishers and name different venues.

editorialLists.name: Time Out
editorialLists.note: HAS NO HOT POT LIST. Three slugs probed 2026-09-03, all 404. Worth re-probing on the next refresh: Time Out publishing one would be the single most valuable addition to this corpus.

editorialLists.name: Eater London
editorialLists.note: HAS NO HOT POT MAP. Two slugs probed 2026-09-03, both 404.

editorialLists.name: SquareMeal
editorialLists.note: HAS NO HOT POT LIST, and beware: SquareMeal returns HTTP 200 for a missing guide, serving a page whose h1 reads 'Best Restaurants not found'. A status code is not a page. Do not record it.

blogAndDiasporaSources.name: Red Scarf 红领巾
blogAndDiasporaSources.note: The most valuable single source on this topic. Chinese-language UK guide, updated April 2026, 19 London venues A-Z with street addresses and per-head price bands. Runs a second page - an annual UK-wide readers' hot pot poll - which is the same domain and therefore the same source; its ranks are carried in quotes and scoped to London first.

blogAndDiasporaSources.name: London Cheapo
blogAndDiasporaSources.note: Added to data/sources.json in this pass. Refuses WebFetch with a 403; read with curl under a browser user agent. Its beginner's guide - cooking times, the two sets of chopsticks, the yin-and-yang divided pot - is the best how-to-eat-it writing found anywhere and is what the article's ordering section rests on.

blogAndDiasporaSources.name: Goldfoil Magazine
blogAndDiasporaSources.note: Added in this pass. Single-venue, independently framed.

blogAndDiasporaSources.name: Hot Dinners
blogAndDiasporaSources.note: No hot pot list, but a news piece on Yangguofu's Chinatown opening.

blogAndDiasporaSources.name: Surrey Chinese
blogAndDiasporaSources.note: STALE, dated 2018. Flagged rather than excluded, per the recency rule. Nothing may be published on its word alone.

facetAxis.note: A NEW AXIS RATHER THAN A SHEET COLUMN, and the only honest choice here. The sheet's existing Setting column is about the room, and hot pot rooms are almost uniformly bright, functional and loud - it would sort thirty venues into one bucket. Specialities has no value that separates a Chongqing mala pot from a Beijing copper pot. Regional style is what the sources themselves organise by, what actually changes the meal, and what decides where a reader should go: someone who wants clear-broth instant-boiled lamb will hate a beef-tallow mala pot and vice versa. The values below are only the ones the corpus can support with named venues; a style with no London venue in the corpus is not listed, however famous it is elsewhere.

values.label: Sichuan and Chongqing mala
values.describeAs: a beef-tallow broth loaded with dried chillies and Sichuan peppercorns, numbing as much as hot, often served in a nine-grid pot

values.label: Beijing copper pot
values.describeAs: clear water in a charcoal-fired copper pot with a chimney up the middle, paper-thin lamb cooked in seconds and dipped in sesame sauce

values.label: Mongolian lamb
values.describeAs: lamb-led, a clear herbal bone broth, and the principle that a good broth should not need a dipping sauce

values.label: Chaoshan and Teochew beef
values.describeAs: a mild beef-bone or clear broth built entirely around hand-cut beef, sorted by cut, where the broth stays out of the way

values.label: Cantonese and seafood bases
values.describeAs: congee, coconut chicken and fish-maw broths, with seafood cooked in them and the broth drunk at the end

values.label: Dongbei and lamb spine
values.describeAs: yang xie zi - stewed lamb spine eaten with your hands, then the pot topped up and used for cooking

values.label: Malatang and maocai
values.describeAs: hot pot's single-serving descendant: you fill a basket from a chilled counter, it is weighed, priced and cooked into one bowl for you

values.label: Taiwanese
values.describeAs: the cheaper all-you-can-eat end, usually attached to a snack-house menu

formatSection.title: The chains, honestly
formatSection.note: Haidilao, Happy Lamb, Da Long Yi, Yangguofu and Shu Xiang Ge are all branches of large Chinese groups, and the guide must be straight about them rather than sneering. The chains genuinely win on the things that decide a first hot pot: they take bookings, they hold walk-in tables, they open late, they hand you an apron and a hair tie and a bag for your coat, they have picture menus and tablet ordering, and their staff will talk a beginner through it. The independents win on specificity - a copper pot, a lamb spine, a particular cut of Chaoshan beef - and usually on price. Say which is which and let the reader choose.

knownGaps: NO JUDGED AWARD EXISTS FOR THIS CATEGORY. Stated plainly in the evidence block. Do not go looking for one again without new information, and do not promote a readers' poll to fill the space.

NO TIER E. Reddit is blocked to the fetcher here and APIFY_TOKEN is not configured, so the community tier could not be collected. TikTok returns only /discover/ aggregate pages, which are search-results pages and never citable. audit-source-mix will show E at zero.
TIER D IS BROAD BUT SHALLOW. Six of seven video sources cover one venue each. The tier supplies independent voices, not comparison.
TWO SOURCES ARE MORE THAN FIVE YEARS OLD (2018 and 2020) and are flagged in the corpus. Their addresses have already drifted once.
HAIDILAO PICCADILLY'S CLOSING TIME IS CONTESTED between two secondary sources (3am vs 11pm) and is not published until the venue's own site confirms it.
CHEF ZHANG XIAOZHONG IS CLAIMED BY BOTH HOTTO POTTO AND TIAN FU. Hotto Potto's own site says he leads it; two editorial sources attribute him to Tian Fu. Not asserted for either.

MOST OF THESE VENUES ARE NEW TO THE SHEET. Almost nothing in this corpus was already on Restaurants v2, so coordinates will be missing until the rows are geocoded, and any venue that cannot be geocoded from its address will be omitted from the map rather than pinned approximately.

PRICE DETAIL IS UNEVEN. Red Scarf gives per-head bands for 19 venues and Hotto Potto publishes a set price on its own site, but most venues do not publish a menu the fetcher can read. Anything printed as a price must be traceable to the venue's own site or to a named source with a date.
openVenueQuestions: Little Sichuan has two different addresses in the corpus - 279C Finchley Road NW3 6LT (2020) and 4-6 Northways Parade, South Hampstead NW3 5EN (2026). Northways Parade is on Finchley Road, so this is probably one venue that moved or was renumbered, but it is recorded as one venue on the newer address and flagged rather than resolved silently.

Shu Xiang Ge has been at 43 New Oxford Street (2018) and is now given as 10 Gerrard Street (2026), with a White City branch named in the 2023 poll. Sources spell it Shu Xiang Ge, Shu Xiangge and Shu Xiang Ge Hot Pot. Merged on the alias list; confirm the current branch count before publishing branch detail.
Hotto Potto and Tian Fu both claim Chef Zhang Xiaozhong. One of them is wrong, or he consults for both. Needs a human decision before either claim is printed.

Little Lamb Hotpot (72 Shaftesbury Avenue) and Joy Luck (47 Gerrard Street) appear only in the 2018 source and in no current one. Likely closed. They are recorded but not published, and are closure candidates for data/closed.json.

Charco Charco is described by London x London as a marriage of hot pot and yakiniku. Whether it belongs in a Chinese hot pot guide or a Japanese one is a judgement call; it is left in the corpus and out of the article's main sections.

Feng Wei Shi Tang is given as 'two London branches' with no addresses by the only source that names it. It is the corpus's clearest Beijing copper-pot recommendation and cannot be mapped until an address is confirmed.
Mr Wang Hot Pot's website (mrwanghotpot.co.uk) did not resolve on 2026-09-03, though it appeared in search results. Confirm the domain before any booking or site link is published for it.
